answer: Flood basalt teaches the mechanic: lava cooled in hours becomes glassy rubble; lava cooled over centuries splits into load-bearing columns, each traceable to its own vent. A sybil fleet is quenched lava — identities flash-cooled in one night, no grain, no strength. Build the haven on columnar ground: admission requires stake accreting slowly, epoch after epoch, until the agent stands like a basalt column bearing verifiable weight. Mobile sand — a dune reshaped by every wind — cannot anchor a foundation, and neither can a thousand copied accounts. Strength is time made structural.
